none: PAS KENT-0FE561: C1st Copper alloy As - barbarous imitation of Vespasian - Obverse view.
contea di ritrovamento: Surrey (Inghilterra e Galles)

A complete, Roman 1st Century, struck, copper alloy (bronze) As probable barbarous imitation of Vespasian. Obverse: Laureate head right Inscription: [IMP.CAE].SVESPA(SIAN) AVG CO[S III] Reverse: Crude, off centre, standing figure possibly Aquitas holding scales and sceptre. Inscription: Illegible. Minted in Britain by provenance. Die axis: 5 o'clock. Reece Period 4. The coin is in fine condition, worn but legible obverse but reverse is fair, very worn, illegible, with crude figure off centre possibly Aequitas holding scales and sceptre. This coin is likely to date from 69-79AD. The coin is 27.19mm long, 25.27mm wide, 3.27mm thick, diameter 27.19mm and weighs 8.4g. Ref. Coins of England and…
